BREAK-EVEN: the budget closes iff the unmeasured 21% of proteome mass has a mean half-life above 2.46 h.
That is 10x below the measured 10th percentile (26 h), so the margin is real -- but this is the
conditional statement, not a bare PASS, and it is the number that falsifies the gate if it is ever measured.
SELF-CONSISTENCY, and it moves the headline. Everything above uses loop 65's
LITERATURE doubling time of 24 h. Loop 71 measured THIS model's own growth at
0.02036 /h -- a 34.04 h doubling. At the model's own rate:
demand/supply          0.4166 at 24 h  ->  0.3296 at 34.0 h   (a slower cell has MORE ribosome-seconds to spend)
replacement fraction   29.2% at 24 h  ->  36.9% at 34.0 h   (and it spends more of them on upkeep)
break-even half-life   2.46 h    ->  2.15 h
So the gate as written is the CONSERVATIVE choice on the budget, but the '29% of the ribosome
budget is replacement' headline is an UNDERSTATEMENT: self-consistently with loop 71 it is 37%.

CORRECTION TO THIS MODULE'S OWN DOCSTRING. The scratch calculation quoted there
gave rho +0.3202 between half-life and fame. That was computed on a pool of 602
genes that was 96% essential -- CEG intersected with measured half-lives -- so it
measured fame WITHIN the essential set, not across the proteome. On the honest
4,595-protein pool the correlation is +0.0590: near zero.
Half-life is NOT a fame proxy. It simply carries almost no essentiality signal,
and adding it to a good baseline dilutes that baseline. Those are different
diagnoses and the record should carry the right one.
